title: You hear your name through any noise

lines.text: In a loud room, you're ignoring every conversation. Then someone says your name, and you hear it instantly.
It's called the cocktail party effect.
In 1953, scientist Colin Cherry played people two messages at once and asked them to follow just one.
People could barely say anything about the message they were ignoring.
But some still caught their own name in it.
Your brain is always quietly scanning the noise for things that matter to you.
Your name is one of the strongest signals it listens for.
So you're never really ignoring the room. Your brain just isn't telling you.
